findings.text: The different-locus reclaim links the retired name onto the revived id (MERGE (tomb)-[:REFINED_FROM]->(old), _RECLAIM_MUTATION_QUERY at edit.py:3341, enabled by link_lineage at edit.py:3451) inside the transaction that commits at edit.py:3460, and the only cycle detection is the readback at edit.py:3495, which raises AFTER that commit. When the renaming name already descends from the tombstone through a live intermediate, the walk returns tips=[M] with M live, M != target, M at the different locus and target at the tombstone's own locus, so the different_locus case is admitted and the write closes tomb -> target -> ... -> M -> tomb. The postflight then raises and leaves the directed cycle plus the revival and retirement committed, so a refused reclaim corrupts the lineage it exists to protect. Repair: refuse before the write when target already descends from the tombstone (the same EXISTS { (target)-[:REFINED_FROM*1..]->(tomb) } shape used at edit.py:3484), or assert the cycle inside the transaction so the rollback undoes it.

_reclaim_successor_tips duplicates the successor-lineage walk the module already owns at edit.py:2041 (_fold_lineage_walk): both descend only through a descendant confirmed superseded, return the live tips, treat a live intermediate as a stopping point, detect a cycle and report an over-depth walk, and even carry near-identical docstring prose. The addition duplicates rather than extends or wraps the owner; it introduces a second bound (_RECLAIM_MAX_DEPTH = 12 at edit.py:3158 against _FOLD_CHAIN_MAX_DEPTH = 64 at edit.py:2028) and a second query path instead of generalising the existing walk. The clone detector at promotion is likely to flag the copied prose.

_RECLAIM_TOMBSTONE_QUERY projects [(succ:StandardName)-[:REFINED_FROM]->(tomb) | succ.id] AS successors, but _reclaim_spelling_case at edit.py:3260 reads only rows[0]['properties'], so every rename attempt against a superseded occupant pays a redundant pattern-comprehension traversal for a field nothing consumes.

The 'Added failures' row states zero and says 'All three ids triaged in one serial run at head pass (6 passed, EXIT=0)', but logs/triage-head.log records 2 tests and '2 passed', and the base arm's 2-failure run that puts test_worker_uses_canonical_model in the base union has no log on disk. Subtracting the reviewed run's own recorded arms (baseline_suite 6 ids from logs/base-default-sn.log against after_suite 4 ids from logs/after-suite-a62c2fc8c.log) leaves one head-only id; the serial triage at both revisions shows it is load-sensitive rather than caused by this change, so the conclusion holds but the figure does not follow from the artefacts the fragment cites.
